purpose: One long-running Plan preserves the complete requested outcome; short bounded workflows execute it incrementally without shrinking the Plan to the current job.
contract: New Plans use starci/plan@2. Existing v1 Plans are readable but do not prove full coverage; never silently migrate their hashes or approvals. A new workflow goal presentation requires an explicitly reviewed v2 Plan.
format: English YAML; present the goal to the user in config.language
stage: Plan preflight: a long-running sequence of bounded workflows, not another workflow or product Work node
beforeApproval: Present business, architecture, implementation, UAT, exclusions and the ordered workflow estimate table
Wait for an actual user reply approving the presented plan

sections.business: Customer outcome, actors, autonomous decisions, policies, normal and exception flows; explain change, reuse or non-applicability.
sections.architecture: Service and data owners, call direction, contracts, authorization, Saga/CQRS and recovery impacts at module level.
sections.implementation: Overall implementation outcome; backend and frontend also have separate coverage rows, even when one is genuinely not applicable. Identify repositories, directories, proposed future targets and quality gates. Freeze current source hashes and exact write ceilings only when presenting the affected workflow goal.
sections.backend: Backend deliverables, API/data contracts and unit/E2E proof, linked to producing workflow IDs; not a vague promise to decide later.
sections.frontend: UI/draw, frontend code and integration deliverables linked to producing workflow IDs; preserve any explicitly requested design alternatives and user selection before implementation.
sections.uat: Named sequential user flows, expected outcomes, evidence and cleanup; distinguish unit/backend E2E from browser UAT.
sections.workflows: The complete ordered route to the terminal outcome: named jobs with purpose, Work targets, proposed path/resource ceilings, prior inputs, outputs, criteria and estimated minutes range with assumptions. Each job is a bounded segment, not a replacement Plan. Unknown future technical details belong to that job's openQuestions and are resolved at its goal checkpoint. Estimates are not promises.

coverage.shape: Each area has action, outcome, targets, workflowIds, evidence and reason. completionCriteria contains unique IDs, observable terminal outcomes and producing workflowIds. All references must resolve to jobs in this Plan.
coverage.change: Required work maps to producing workflows even when execution is later or currently blocked. Lack of current approval never removes an end-to-end stage.
coverage.reuse: Reuse identifies existing target and evidence references, not a future decision or a no-write permission. Validators check declared references structurally, not their truth; inspect actual evidence before relying on reuse.
coverage.notApplicable: Use only with an explicit scope reason. No frontend in a CLI-only repair can be legitimate; frontend not yet approved in a requested application is not non-applicability.
coverage.planningOnly: When asked only to plan a product, still describe the whole intended business, architecture, backend, frontend and UAT route. Planning or presenting future implementation jobs does not authorize executing them.
coverage.boundedRequests: A genuinely narrow maintenance, design-only or content request needs complete coverage of its own outcome, not invented product stages. Do not pad every Plan with all workflow types.
coverage.blockers: Show which job is blocked and keep the product goal, downstream stages and terminal criteria visible. A separately authorized runtime repair is a prerequisite intervention, never the product Plan or evidence that the product shipped.

approval: A task-creation prompt, original request, assistant message, silence or self-authored receipt never approves a subsequently presented goal. Bind the actual later user reply to the presented scope and goal. Local scripts cannot authenticate a human; preserve real host message provenance.
sequence: Execute listed jobs in order within one Plan bundle. Present and confirm each bounded workflow goal in its own task, execute its operators, verify the result and obtain acceptance before handing off. Pass only accepted typed outputs unchanged. A Plan is not complete because one workflow is done; every planned job and terminal criterion must be satisfied. Observers receive status, not approval authority. Planning approval never accepts future results or authorizes unresolved effects.
questions: Plan.openQuestions concern the terminal scope and block all goal approvals. job.openQuestions concern only that future workflow and must remain visible without blocking earlier independent jobs. At its checkpoint, bind exact question/answer pairs in goal.inputs.planQuestionAnswers and present them with the workflow goal; actual goal approval covers those answers. Do not mutate the original Plan or migrate old receipts merely to record those answers. Answers that change the terminal scope or approved effect ceiling require explicit Plan revision instead.
changes: Business, service, authorization, schema, targets or effect-ceiling changes invalidate the affected approval and require a revised user-facing goal.
cleanup: Keep unfinished or failed scope/session drafts for resumption. After all jobs are accepted and canonical Work proof validates, remove only this scope's temporary files and owned sessions. Preserve current product evidence in Work; Git tracks product history. Never recursively delete a shared session root.
legacy: Already running jobs without a presented goal must pause and present their current changes and revised scope; never manufacture retroactive approval.
ownership: Backend owns .starci and canonical .work; frontend resolves them through workspace bindings. Keep .starci local and ignored by Git.

files.index.yaml: Stable Plan ID and relative pointers only; no duplicate execution state.
files.goal/index.yaml: The whole ordered Plan plus exact current workflow goals, their bindings and digests. No history.
files.approval/index.yaml: Pending or actual user decision receipts for each presented goal/result; bind message provenance and hashes. Never infer approval from a task request.
files.run/index.yaml: Current job states, requests, accepted responses, typed handoffs and evidence references. Preserve every completed producer needed by later jobs. No attempt history.

storage: One backend-owned .starci/plans/<plan-id>/ bundle. All workflows in the same Plan share this directory; never create a separate runs tree or a new Plan per workflow.
recovery: Incomplete writes or mismatched Plan digests block resumption; never treat file presence as approval. Keep unfinished bundles. Goal revisions require renewed approval, not overwriting a running goal.
presentation: Mandatory terminal Goal, areas including backend/frontend, coverage with reuse evidence/non-applicability reasons, Plan completion criteria, ordered workflows with input/output/criteria/estimate, per-workflow checkpoints, exclusions and pending approval. Keep future jobs visible when presenting the current workflow. Translate display prose to config.language. Draft-only trials use the same bundle in an allowed scratch location.

selection.facts: Each job requires selection.requestQuote (exact original request excerpt), codeChange, verification (none/unit-component/browser-uat), separateDeliverable.
selection.backend: Do not schedule implementation just to inspect API evidence.
selection.frontend: Includes draw/reuse and browser UAT; duplicate standalone jobs require explicit separate intent.
selection.verification: verify-flows is browser UAT, never a renamed unit/component check. Use review-code for inspecting existing implementation/test coverage.
selection.scope: Missing features do not authorize adding requirements. Record unresolved interpretations in openQuestions and resolve before approval.
selection.trust: Structural validators reject inconsistent declared facts; the coordinator must still compare them to user intent and evidence. Never assert semantic correctness solely from schema validity.
